claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'd like to ask you a few questions about Alex to determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in school, college, sixth form, or doing an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in school anymore. He's actually started an apprenticeship up in Aberdeen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify one important detail:

**Is Alex's apprenticeship in England, or is it in Scotland?** (You mentioned it's in Aberdeen, which is in Scotland - I just want to confirm this is correct.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - it's in Aberdeen, Scotland.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Based on the information you've provided, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the situation:
- Alex is 17 years old
- He lives at home with you in the UK
- He has started an apprenticeship in Scotland (Aberdeen)

According to the Child Benefit rules, you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts an apprenticeship in England. However, the rule specifically mentions apprenticeships **in England**.

Since Alex's apprenticeship is in Scotland (not England), this specific exclusion rule doesn't directly apply. However, I need one more piece of information to make a final determination:

**Is Alex working 24 hours or more a week in his apprenticeship, and has he left all approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's working full-time in the apprenticeship - it's a proper full-time position.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information.

Based on everything you've told me, I now have sufficient information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me summarize the situation:
- Alex is 17 years old
- He lives at home with you in the UK
- He has started a full-time apprenticeship in Scotland (Aberdeen), working 24+ hours per week
- He is no longer in approved education or training

According to the Child Benefit rules, you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training. While the rules specifically mention that you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child "starts an apprenticeship in England," the broader rule about working 24+ hours per week while not in approved education or training applies regardless of location within the UK.

Since Alex is working full-time (24+ hours per week) and is no longer in approved education or training, you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for him.

If you're currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, you should inform HMRC about this change in circumstances as soon as possible.
